text.p: The following are the main stories from Tuesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Milk producer NOeM plans to start a strategical partnership with Italy's Parmalat. The company also plans to cooperate more closely with another major Austrian milk producer Berglandmilch.

- The option for Germany's Westdeutsche Landesbank to take over the City of Vienna's 49 percent voting stake in Bank Austria ends by the year 2001. So the privatisation of Bank Austria is expected to take place after that.

- A boycott of all work in parliamentary committees by opposition parties has shown first results after all the party leaders met yesterday. A reform of the procedures of investigative committees is now planned.

- Social Democrat chief whip Peter Kostelka is strictly against plans for Austria to join NATO. He says the coalition partner the People's Party should rather return to Austria's policy of active foreign politics.
- The number of illegal immigrants caught at the border nearly doubled to 5,058 in the first five months of 1997.
- 10,000 civil servants in the Finance Ministry stage a warning strike today against planned austerity measures. Delays are only expected to result in customs.
- Future privatisations will have to be accepted by the government twice in order to be realised.

- Steelmaker VA Stahl sees an increase in demand and expects prices to rise slowly. A dividend of 15 schillings will be paid out for 1996 and the first quarter of 1997, as the company changes its financial year.
DIE PRESSE

- Conservatives are outraged about Westdeutsche Landesbank's (WestLB) buy option for Bank Austria. They say they were not told about it when they agreed on Bank Austria taking over Creditanstalt. They demand the sale must be revoked should WestLB not renounce its option.
- At least eight member countries of the European Union are in favour of an EU-wide resource tax to be introduced by 1998.
KURIER
- Austria is of special importance for NATO due to the eastward expansion of the military alliance, its commander-in-chief George Joulwan says.
- Constructor Era-Bau has received the order to renovate Moscow's Kremlin for 750 million schillings.
- The new telecommunications law, which is supposed to protect smaller telecommunications providers from the current monopoly Post & Telekom Austria, should pass the council of ministers today.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- 40 billion schillings are still missing for the budget of 1998. Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger says spending will have to be reduced before new taxes will be introduced.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Chamber of Economy expects exporters and importers to save up to 50 billion schillings through the introduction of Europe's single currency euro.
